classification.difficultyReason: Find an acute angle using the sine rule, obtain the remaining angle and use it as the included angle in the area rule.

content.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$ shown, $\angle CAB$ is an acute angle.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with A above, C at the lower left and B at the lower right. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black under house style. The source prints the angle value without an angle arc.
spec.mathematics: AB = 16 cm, CB = 20 cm, angle ACB = 50 degrees; angle CAB is acute.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the sine rule to find $\angle CAB$, correct to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{20}{\sin\angle CAB}&=\frac{16}{\sin50^\circ}\\\frac{\sin\angle CAB}{20}&=\frac{\sin50^\circ}{16}\\\sin\angle CAB&=\frac{20\sin50^\circ}{16}\\\angle CAB&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{20\sin50^\circ}{16}\right)\\\angle CAB&\approx73.2^\circ\end{align*}$$
The acute solution is required.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find $\angle ABC$, correct to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$. Using the unrounded result from part a:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=180^\circ-50^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{20\sin50^\circ}{16}\right)\\\angle ABC&\approx56.8^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the area of the triangle, correct to the nearest square centimetre.

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded value of $\angle ABC$, the included angle between the known sides.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\frac12\times16\times20\times\sin\angle ABC\\\text{Area}&=160\sin\left(130^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{20\sin50^\circ}{16}\right)\right)\\\text{Area}&\approx134\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
